title: Finishing a Game
intro: A full game counts surrounded empty points and prisoners. These small positions show a final move, passing, and checking the score.

steps.instruction: Inspect Black, then the white stone at F3.

proofs.caption: White cannot fill either B3 or D3: neither move captures Black, and each would have no liberty. These two separate eyes keep Black alive.
White tries F2 and is refused: it captures nothing and leaves the white group with no liberty.
Black plays F2 and captures White F3. This group cannot escape. The next example restores it so we can inspect the count.

steps.explanation: Black has two separate empty pockets. White cannot fill its last liberty at F2: that captures nothing and leaves White without a liberty. Black could capture at F2. This white stone cannot escape.

steps.instruction: This boundary is still open. Close it to protect the two empty points below.
steps.hint: A4 closes the gap. Filling a pocket would spend your territory.
steps.explanation: A4 closes the boundary around A3 and B3. White passes. Filling your secure empty points would reduce your territory.

steps.instruction: Both boundaries are closed. Pass with P to offer to finish.
steps.explanation: White passes too. Two passes start counting. A pass does not concede; an opponent may instead play another move.

steps.instruction: Click White F3 twice to compare the mark. Restore it, then confirm with P.
steps.explanation: Marked White F3 adds one prisoner and opens F3 and F2 as territory. Black has 5 territory + 1 prisoner. White has 2 territory + 0.5 komi. Only agreed dead stones are removed.

outro: In your practice game, Help can point out liberties. At the count, inspect the proposed marks before accepting.
